evidence.description: Successful credential clearing resets regular tokens but does not clear ssoCredentials.
The token setup helper updates authentication tokens and login status without resetting cached SSO credentials.
Cookie creation uses the cached SSO credentials whenever the service is logged in.

candidates.explanation: SSO credentials remain cached after logout and subsequent login. Until another SSO retrieval completes, cookie creation can reuse the previous session's transfer token, including after signing in with a different account.
candidates.title: SSO credentials survive logout and account changes

evidence.description: Local tokens and login status are reset only when clearCredentials returns true.
When credential clearing fails, no error is thrown if there is no session error and credentials cannot be renewed.

candidates.explanation: If clearCredentials returns false, session clearing has not failed, and canRenewCredentials returns false, logout returns normally without resetting in-memory tokens, the profile, or isLoggedIn. Non-renewability does not establish that the service's existing authentication state has been cleared.
candidates.title: Logout can return successfully without clearing local authentication

evidence.description: Tokens are cleared before a throwing image-cache operation, while profile clearing occurs only after that operation succeeds.

candidates.explanation: An error from ImageCacheLoader.clearCache escapes logout after credentials and tokens have already been cleared but before userProfile is reset. This leaves the previous user's profile exposed in an otherwise logged-out service and reports logout failure because of ancillary cache cleanup.
candidates.title: Image-cache failure interrupts logout state cleanup

evidence.description: The explicit credentialsStorageFailed error is thrown inside the same do block whose catch wraps every error as credentialsStorageError.

candidates.explanation: When storeCredentials returns false, the credentialsStorageFailed error is immediately caught and wrapped in credentialsStorageError. Callers cannot receive the distinct failure case directly, even though the method distinguishes a false return from a thrown storage error.
candidates.title: Credential-storage failure is caught and wrapped as a different error

evidence.description: An informational log includes the user's name, email address, and profile-picture URL.

candidates.explanation: Routine authentication logging copies identifiable profile data into logs. This expands the exposure of personal information beyond the profile state itself, including through any collection or retention of those logs.
candidates.title: Successful profile retrieval logs personal information
